Custom tools for insurers and reinsurers

Source: vignettes/articles/custom-tools.Rmd
custom-tools.Rmd

NetSimR and its six tools are free. The same approach — actuarial methods validated against established packages, in tools that people who do not write R can use — can be built around your own data, assumptions and processes.

Pricing

GLM rating models, rate tables ready for a rating engine, scoring of new business, and rate reviews with on-levelling, trend and credibility.

Reserving, IFRS 17 and Solvency II

Reserving tools on your triangles, with discounting, the risk adjustment, the standard formula's reserve risk, and reports for the reserving committee.

Reinsurance

Experience and exposure rating of treaties, and the comparison of programmes by their cost and the capital they save.

Capital

Simulation of the portfolio's lines with their dependence, capital by line, and the comparison with the standard formula.

How the work is done

  • Your data, where it lives: databases, Excel workbooks or files, read as they are.
  • Your data stays yours: a tool runs on your own servers or on each actuary’s computer, and sends nothing outside, as NetSimR’s tools do.
  • Your methods and assumptions: the tool does what your actuaries do today, faster and the same way every time, with the choices they make in it recorded.
  • Validated: results checked against established packages and hand calculations, with automated tests, as NetSimR’s are.
  • Documented: reports that explain the figures to a committee, an auditor or a regulator.
  • Delivered the way you work: a tool in the browser, on your own servers or on each actuary’s computer, or an R package for your team, with training and a handover.

See the tools

The Try online page runs NetSimR’s six tools in your browser, and its gallery shows them at work. A worked example runs each tool on example data and opens the report it writes, the kind of document a custom tool hands to a committee. The vignette From pricing to capital and reserves follows one portfolio through the same steps in code.
